title: Suspicious process spawned by a web server
description: Detects command interpreters and administrative utilities spawned directly by common web-server processes.

hypothesis.summary: A compromised web application or web shell may launch a command interpreter or administrative utility from its web-server worker process.
hypothesis.rationale: Microsoft identifies abnormal child processes of IIS workers as a useful web-shell signal, MITRE describes web shells as a persistence mechanism and SigmaHQ maintains a comparable process-creation analytic; some applications legitimately launch child tools.
hypothesis.detection_goal: Identify selected command interpreters and administrative utilities whose direct initiating process is a common web server while leaving ordinary web-server child processes and the same tools from unrelated parents unmatched.

data_sources.name: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint process events

triage.summary: Establish whether the parent is an expected web workload, then investigate the child command and any related web-facing activity as a possible post-exploitation chain.
steps: Review the parent and child image, complete command line, account, device role and application-pool or service context.
Correlate the process with inbound web requests, recent web-root or configuration changes, module loads and files created by the web-server process.
Confirm any documented application behavior with the service owner; isolate the server and preserve web and endpoint evidence when the child process is unexplained.
false_positives: Approved web applications, deployment agents, monitoring components or server-management workflows that intentionally launch the selected tools

validation.expected_outcome: Match selected command and administrative child processes from common web servers; do not match ordinary children, unrelated parents or unsupported web-server processes.
